slo_note: LOCAL-ONLY foundation/data-infra story. No deployed service, no HTTP endpoints, no production runtime. SLOs (p95 < 200ms, max regression 20%) cannot be measured and are NOT-APPLICABLE for this stage.

findings.description: seed.ts inserts employees and their EmployeeSkill rows sequentially in a loop (one INSERT per employee, one INSERT per skill-assignment per employee). This is a seed/migration path — not a hot query path — and runs once at setup time with 22 profiles. No runtime impact.
findings.recommendation: Acceptable for a one-shot seed of 22 records. If the seed grows to thousands of profiles, batch with createMany inside a $transaction for speed. No action needed for SKILL-1.

findings.description: resolveCanonicalSkill (Layer 2 path) calls prisma.skill.findMany to fetch all canonical keys before passing them to Claude. For SKILL-1's expected catalog size (12 skills seeded) this is negligible. At scale (hundreds of skills) this becomes an unbounded full-table scan on every unknown skill.
findings.recommendation: Advisory only. When the skill catalog grows, cache the canonical-key list in memory (or use a Redis SET) rather than re-fetching on every Layer-2 call. Not a blocking concern for the hackathon demo.

findings.category: No explicit indexes on FK columns (SQLite advisory)
findings.description: SQLite does NOT auto-index foreign key columns. The following FK columns in the schema lack explicit @@index declarations: EmployeeSkill.employeeId, EmployeeSkill.skillId, Enrollment.employeeId, Enrollment.catalogItemId, Certificate.employeeId, Resume.employeeId, PlanItem.planId, PlanItem.catalogItemId, UpskillingPlan.employeeId (covered by @unique), IdentityMapping.employeeId (covered by @unique). Queries that filter by these columns (e.g. 'fetch all skills for an employee') will do a full table scan in SQLite without an index.
findings.recommendation: Add @@index([employeeId]) to EmployeeSkill, Enrollment, Certificate, Resume, and PlanItem. For a hackathon demo with 22 seed profiles this is below detection threshold. Recommend adding indexes before any real-scale demo or production use to avoid O(N) scans on skill lookups and cert fetches. This is advisory — not a gate failure for SKILL-1.

findings.description: The self-referencing leadId FK on Employee is not indexed. 'Fetch all team members for a Practice Lead' will scan all employees. With 22 seed profiles this is negligible.
findings.recommendation: Add @@index([leadId]) to Employee when the team size grows. Advisory only.

findings.category: No resource leak — Prisma client lifecycle correct
findings.description: db.ts uses a globalThis singleton to reuse the Prisma client across Next.js hot-reloads (standard pattern). seed.ts instantiates its own client and explicitly calls prisma.$disconnect() in both the success and error paths. No unclosed handle detected.

gate_details.n_plus_1_hot_path: PASS — no N+1 in a hot/runtime query path. The seed loop is a one-shot init path.
gate_details.missing_index_single_record_invariant: PASS — the single-record invariant (BR-18) is enforced by @@unique([employeeId, skillId]) on EmployeeSkill and @unique on UpskillingPlan.employeeId. Both are indexed by the UNIQUE constraint in SQLite.
gate_details.resource_leaks: PASS — no unclosed Prisma clients or DB handles detected.
gate_details.atomicity_violations: PASS — no read-then-write races on the same entity without a guard. upsertAndPromoteSkill's read+conditional-write is acceptable: the @@unique constraint + the sequential SQLite write serializer prevents a duplicate row; the worst case of a race is a benign re-read after a unique-violation catch (see resolveCanonicalSkill lines 93-102).
gate_details.performance_tests_required: NOT-APPLICABLE — LOCAL-ONLY foundation story; no deployed service surface.
gate_details.slo_runtime_validation: DEFERRED — to Tier 2/3 when a runnable service exists (not in scope for SKILL-1).
